title: Per-action-class reversibility (ACP-SPEC-001 §9.6, RV-1)
description:
Maps each action class to whether it can be undone.

RV-1: an action ABSENT from this file MUST be treated as IRREVERSIBLE. As with floors, JSON Schema cannot express absence, so the rule is carried by the `x-acp-absent` annotation below and GENERATED into the type: `impl Default for Reversibility` returns `Irreversible` in crates/acp-core, and the lookup on the table returns it directly, so a struct update, a deserialisation gap, or an `Option` a caller unwraps cannot silently produce the permissive value.

Why this matters more than it looks: reversibility selects the acknowledgement regime. IRREVERSIBLE at floor-HIGH demands positive acknowledgement from a non-operator (DR-9) — silence is not consent. Getting this entry wrong in the permissive direction converts a held action into a released one.

RV-3 is the reason the value is recomputed here and never read from a receipt: a compromised issuer claiming REVERSIBLE otherwise obtains Silent mode. Proven in reference/proofs/binding.dfy as `RV3_TrustedModeAcceptsDowngrade`.

A-7 applies here exactly as it does to floors: that a classification is HONEST is conceded unprovable.

reversibility.description: action class -> reversibility. Open map (actions are deployment-specific), closed values.

x-acp-absent.why: reversibility selects the acknowledgement regime, so the permissive default converts a held action into a released one. An action nobody classified is one nobody thought about, and the fail-safe reading of that is that it cannot be undone.

reversibility.description:
Whether an action class can be undone.

Hoisted out of `additionalProperties` into `$defs` so that it has a NAME. An inline enum is a type the generator has to invent a name for, and an invented name is a name that drifts — `floors.schema.json` already declared its values under `$defs.tier` and this file did not, which is a difference with no reason behind it.

DELIBERATELY NOT ORDERED. REVERSIBLE and IRREVERSIBLE are two cases, not a scale; a generated `Ord` would invite `max` composition that means nothing here.
